response.title: what solar generator should i buy for my elderly parents who are not technical
response.answer:
For elderly parents who aren't comfortable with technology, I would prioritize simplicity, reliability, and safety over maximum power or fancy features.

My recommendation is to buy a portable power station from EcoFlow, Jackery, or Anker SOLIX, ideally with a LiFePO4 (LFP) battery.

One important distinction: a solar generator is essentially a large rechargeable battery. Solar panels are optional, and for your parents, I would actually recommend starting without solar panels. They can simply charge it from a wall outlet and use it during power outages.

What matters most for elderly parents

Easy operation: Plug appliances directly into clearly labeled outlets, without needing a phone app.

Automatic backup: If they rely on something that must stay powered, look for a model with UPS/EPS functionality, while checking whether its transfer time is suitable.

Manageable weight: A 25-pound unit is much easier to move than a 60-pound one.

Low maintenance: LFP batteries generally last longer and require less attention.

Enough capacity: Around 1,000Wh is a good starting point for lights, phones, a router, and other small essentials.

I would avoid complicated whole-home systems unless you plan to have them professionally installed.

For elderly parents, I would also set up the unit in a fixed, accessible location, label the essential plugs, and practice an outage with them once.
